snip.t: Tuberous sclerosis complex (TSC) is a multisystem disease characterized by an autosomal dominant mode of inheritance, variable expressivity, and a prevalence of 1 in 6,000 to 10,000 newborns.

Vigabatrin can be used as a first-line agent for the treatment of infantile spasms in patients with tuberous sclerosis and is the second-line choice if hormonal therapy was unsuccessful in other cases of infantile spasms.

The ketogenic diet is believed to be effective in glucose transporter protein 1 deficiency, pyruvate dehydrogenase deficiency, myoclonic-astatic epilepsy, tuberous sclerosis complex, Rett syndrome, severe myoclonic epilepsy of infancy (Dravet syndrome), and infantile spasms.
Zollinger-Ellison syndrome is common in patients with multiple endocrine neoplasia 1 and rare with neurofibromatosis and tuberous sclerosis.
Tuberous sclerosis causes epilepsy, learning disability, ash-leaf macules, shagreen patches and facial angiofibromas.

qs.q: A 32-year-old woman with a history of tuberous sclerosis is found to have a 5 cm asymptomatic solid renal lesion that shows macroscopic fat density on computed tomography. What is the most likely diagnosis?
qs.e: Angiomyolipomas are benign renal lesions characterised by the presence of fat on CT and are strongly associated with tuberous sclerosis. They carry a risk of bleeding when larger than 4 cm, unlike malignant renal carcinomas.
